problem:
A body of mass $1.5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-12{t}^{2}+t-5$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=6{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}-36t+2$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
feedback.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}-36t+2) \\  & =18{t}^{2}-18t-36\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}18{t}^{2}-18t-36 & =0 \\ {t}^{2}-t-2 & =0 \\ (t+1)(t-2) & =0 \\ t & =-1,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=2\,\text{s}.$
